reason: The support is the complement of the union U of open mu-null sets. In the second-countable plane, the rational open squares with zero mass form a countable family N, and each point of U lies in some B in N: choose a basis square B inside an open null neighborhood and use monotonicity derived from countable additivity to get mu(B)=0. Conversely every B in N lies in U. Thus U is a countable union of null sets and is null by countable subadditivity derived from the measure axiom; its complement is closed and carries mu. Every closed carrier F has C\F open and null, hence C\F is contained in U, so supp(mu) is contained in F and is the smallest closed carrier. Therefore mu is nonzero iff supp(mu) is nonempty, and mu is carried by a compact K iff supp(mu) is compact. The cited Saff footnote gives the equivalent neighborhood-positive support convention.
